newsitem.title: POLAND: Better investment terms in Polish economic zones.
newsitem.headline: Better investment terms in Polish economic zones.

text.p: The Polish government on Tuesday approved a regulation improving terms of foreign investment in two special economic zones, it said in a statement.

Under the new rules, investors would no longer be obliged to manufacture at least 30 percent of components needed for their final products inside the zone to be granted a break on the country's 38 percent corporate tax.

Economy Minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek earlier said that under the regulation the amount of parts that has to be made inside the zone would be subject to individual negotiations between an investor and his ministry.
"This should attract many new investors and facilitate the launch of planned investments, which often require imports of costly, high-tech components," Kaczmarek said late on Monday.

The regulation applies to zones in the northern province of Suwalki and southern province of Katowice, where General Motors' German subsidiary Adam Opel AG is building a 500 million mark car assembly factory.
Under a government programme the zones offer tax breaks for up to 20 years and other investment incentives to create new jobs in areas striken by unemployment.
